text:
If Nomsa (an illustration) spent R1,000 a month on electricity, a 9% increase makes the same electricity cost about R1,090: about R90 more a month, almost R1,100 more a year, for the same lights and the same kettle. On a R12,000 salary, R1,000 is just over 8% of her pay. If electricity keeps rising 9% a year and her pay rises 5% a year, after five years electricity takes about 10% of her pay.

About the example: R1,000 x 1.09 = R1,090. Five years at +9% (electricity) and +5% (pay): R1,538.62 / R15,315.38 = 10.05%.

Full guide: "How Eskom Went Broke, and What It Costs You Every Month (South Africa 2026)" on the Money From Zero channel.
